title: Best CRM for Agencies 2026
description: Compare HubSpot (4.7/5), Salesforce (4.3/5) by client and stakeholder management, pipeline flexibility for service sales, project management integration. Stored ratings are editorial indicators; verify current capabilities, plan limits, and total cost before choosing.
useCaseDescription: Agencies face a unique CRM challenge — they need to manage not just a sales pipeline of prospective clients, but also track ongoing project scopes, retainer agreements, upsell opportunities, and client communication across multiple accounts. Unlike product companies that sell standardized solutions, agencies sell services that are customized to each client, requiring flexible deal structures, custom quotes, and project-based billing. The ideal agency CRM handles contact management for multiple stakeholders per client, tracks proposals and estimates, integrates with project management tools for seamless handoff from sales to delivery, and provides visibility into client health and account growth. Agencies also benefit from CRM features like pipeline reporting by service line, email tracking for proposal follow-ups, and automated reminders for contract renewals and quarterly business reviews. Integration with accounting software for invoicing and time tracking is essential for agencies that bill by the hour or on retainer.

faqs.question: What's the difference between agency CRM and standard CRM?
faqs.answer: Agency CRM needs additional capabilities beyond standard sales CRM: multi-stakeholder account management (multiple contacts per client with different roles), project scope and estimate tracking, retainer and recurring revenue management, handoff workflows from sales to delivery teams, and integration with time tracking and project management tools. Agencies sell services, not products, so the CRM must handle custom quotes, SOWs, and project-based billing.

faqs.question: How should agencies track retainer clients in CRM?
faqs.answer: Retainer clients can be tracked as recurring opportunities with renewal dates, monthly value, and scope documentation. Create a custom deal stage for 'Active Retainer' and use recurring tasks or automated workflows for quarterly business reviews, monthly reporting, and renewal reminders. HubSpot's recurring revenue reporting and Salesforce's opportunity splitting are particularly useful for retainer management.

faqs.question: What integrations do agencies need most from their CRM?
faqs.answer: The most critical integrations for agencies are: email (Gmail/Outlook) for tracking client communications, project management (Asana, Monday.com, Jira) for sales-to-delivery handoff, accounting (QuickBooks, Xero) for invoicing and time tracking, and proposal tools for seamless quote-to-cash workflows. Slack integration also helps keep the team updated on deal progress and client communications.

faqs.question: Can a single CRM work for both new business and account management?
faqs.answer: Yes, the best agency CRMs handle both new business pipeline and existing account management in a single platform. Use separate pipelines or deal stages for prospects vs. active clients. Associate closed-won deals with the client account and create recurring opportunities for upsells, cross-sells, and renewals. This unified approach gives agency leadership complete visibility from first contact through ongoing account growth.

body:
Best CRM for Agencies 2026

Editorial scope: This is a use-case-based buying guide, not a paid ranking or a claim that one vendor wins for every team. Stored ratings and recommendations are decision aids, not independently verified current product evidence. Confirm capabilities, plan limits, data handling, and pricing directly with each vendor before purchase.

Agencies face a unique CRM challenge — they need to manage not just a sales pipeline of prospective clients, but also track ongoing project scopes, retainer agreements, upsell opportunities, and client communication across multiple accounts. Unlike product companies that sell standardized solutions, agencies sell services that are customized to each client, requiring flexible deal structures, custom quotes, and project-based billing. The ideal agency CRM handles contact management for multiple stakeholders per client, tracks proposals and estimates, integrates with project management tools for seamless handoff from sales to delivery, and provides visibility into client health and account growth. Agencies also benefit from CRM features like pipeline reporting by service line, email tracking for proposal follow-ups, and automated reminders for contract renewals and quarterly business reviews. Integration with accounting software for invoicing and time tracking is essential for agencies that bill by the hour or on retainer.

Shortlist to evaluate

Treat these options as candidates to test against the same requirements. Product names, plan packaging, and capabilities can change; do not assume a feature is included in every plan.

  • HubSpot

    Full-service agencies managing pipeline and client relationships

    • Custom deal stages for agency workflows
    • Email tracking and meeting scheduling
    • Quotes and proposal management
    • Client portal and shared documents

    Verify: confirm current availability, limits, integrations, and commercial terms with the vendor; test the workflow before relying on this candidate.

  • Salesforce

    Evaluate Salesforce against the same representative tasks, integrations, plan limits, and operating constraints.

    • Custom objects for retainer and project tracking
    • Advanced forecasting by service line
    • Partner relationship management
    • Einstein AI for upsell predictions

    Verify: confirm current availability, limits, integrations, and commercial terms with the vendor; test the workflow before relying on this candidate.

Selection criteria

Prioritize requirements before comparing feature lists. Separate mandatory requirements from preferences, and record the evidence used to make each decision.

  1. Client and stakeholder management (Critical): Ability to track multiple contacts per client account with relationship mapping, stakeholder roles, and communication history across the full account lifecycle
  2. Pipeline flexibility for service sales (Critical): Customizable deal stages that reflect agency sales cycles from RFP response through proposal, pitch, negotiation, and onboarding, with support for retainer and project-based pricing
  3. Project management integration (High): Seamless handoff from closed-won deals to project delivery tools with automated project creation, scope documentation, and timeline tracking
  4. Proposal and quote management (High): Built-in proposal creation with templates, approval workflows for pricing and discounts, and the ability to track proposal status and follow-up activities
  5. Reporting on account growth and retention (High): Visibility into account expansion, renewals, upsell opportunities, and client health scores to proactively manage agency revenue and retention

How to run a fair pilot

  1. Map the current process from lead capture through qualification, follow-up, opportunity, and closed outcomes.
  2. Test representative contacts, duplicates, pipeline stages, tasks, email/calendar links, reporting, and data import/export.
  3. Verify roles, permissions, automation limits, integration behavior, and how records are exported if the team changes systems.
  4. Measure the effort needed to keep records clean and reports trustworthy; identify who owns data quality and administration.
  5. Compare total cost for the actual seats, required modules, onboarding, and growth plans.

Common pitfalls

  • Using a CRM designed for product sales that can't handle retainer billing, project scoping, and the consultative sales approach typical of agency-client relationships
  • Failing to integrate CRM with project management and time tracking tools, creating manual handoffs that lose context and delay project kickoffs for new clients
  • Not tracking multiple stakeholders per account, missing key decision-makers and influencers in complex agency buying processes
  • Overlooking contract renewal and retainer management features, letting recurring revenue slip through the cracks without automated renewal reminders

Calculate the full cost

Compare subscription and renewal price, seats or users, usage limits, required add-ons, implementation and migration, training, integrations, ongoing administration, and the staff time needed to maintain the workflow. Use the same usage scenario for each candidate and ask vendors to confirm important limits in writing.

Decision checklist

  • Every must-have requirement has a documented test or current vendor source.
  • Unknown capabilities and plan limits are marked unknown rather than assumed.
  • Data export, access control, failure handling, and exit steps have been reviewed.
  • The team has recorded trade-offs, recurring ownership, and expected total cost.
  • The choice reflects the team's workflow rather than a universal ranking.

Revisit the decision when workload, required integrations, operating constraints, or vendor terms change.
